questions.question: What is the physical meaning of real power in household appliances?
questions.solution_html:
• • Real power (P), measured in Watts (W), is the actual power dissipated by a load to
  • perform useful work. It is the component where energy is transformed into another
  • form.
  • • In appliances like irons or heaters, real power represents the heat generated. In
  • motors, it represents the mechanical torque produced. It differs from reactive power
  • which merely cycles between the source and load.
  • • Formula : P=V I cosϕ, where cosϕ is the power factor.
  • (any two relevant points (5 marks). (2.5 marks) mark for 1 point)

questions.question: Match with the best option. / Charge (i) Energy (B) potential difference (ii) temperature power (iii) current (D) volt x ampere (iv) voltage resistance (v) watt
questions.solution_html:
• Match with the best option.
  • • (i) Energy → (D) Volt × Ampere × Time: Energy is power multiplied by time.
  • ((1 Mark))
  • • (ii) Temperature → (E) Resistance: Resistance of most conductors changes with
  • temperature. ((1 Mark))
  • • (iii) Current → (A) Charge: Current is the rate of flow of electric charge. ((1 Mark))
  • • (iv) Voltage → (B) Potential difference: Voltage is the work to move a unit charge.
  • ((1 Mark))
  • • (v) Watt → (C) Power: The SI unit of power. ((1 Mark))
questions.final_answer: Option (d) Volt × Ampere × Time: Energy is power multiplied by time.

questions.question: Explain the response of a capacitor when connected to DC and AC sources.
questions.solution_html:
• • A capacitor blocks steady-state DC current after charging, acting as an open circuit.
  • • In AC, the capacitor continuously charges and discharges as polarity reverses
  • allowing current to "pass."

questions.question: / a) knife switch b) Rotary switch c) isolator
questions.solution_html:
• Rotary switch c) isolator
  • • a) Knife Switch ((2 Marks)): A manual switch with a hinged metal blade. Closing the
  • blade into the slot completes the circuit.
  • • b) Rotary Switch ((1.5 Marks)): Operates by rotating a central spindle to select
  • between multiple circuit paths.
  • • c) Isolator ((1.5 Marks)): A mechanical device used to isolate a circuit for
  • maintenance, operated under "no-load" conditions.

questions.question: Describe the colour code of wires used in an extension board and explain the / significance of each wire.
questions.solution_html:
• • Phase/Live ((2 Marks)): Red or Brown. Carries current from source to appliance.
  • • Neutral ((1.5 Marks)): Black or Blue. Provides the return path to complete the circuit.
  • • Earth/Ground ((1.5 Marks)): Green or Yellow. Safety wire preventing shock by
  • grounding fault currents.
